## Appearance

Paul Irving is a remarkably tall youth with a beautiful face and serious blue eyes. As a boy, he had chestnut brown curls, though these were later replaced by close-cropped brown locks. By his later youth, he has grown into a splendid six-foot figure.

_Sources: [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P30](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0030), [v3 ch.People P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v3 ch.People P13](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0013), [v3 ch.Revelation P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002), [v4 CHAPTER 3 THE LAND OF DREAMS AMONG P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)_

## Personality

Paul Irving is a fair-minded, cleanly, and exceptionally imaginative individual regarded as a genius and a perfect little gentleman. Though noted for his dreams and poetic fancies, he is also very manly and capable of holding his own in games. He possesses a talent for telling stories and writing verse that magazine editors appreciate, and he is driven to go abroad for two years of study.

_Sources: [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P7](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0007), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P32](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0032), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 XI Facts and Fancies P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road P3](../source/v02-c18.md#nw-v02-c18-p0003), [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P33](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0033), +4 more_

## History

Paul Irving was a motherless boy who lived down near the shore with his grandmother and only grew acquainted with his father after his mother died three years prior. As an imaginative student in [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) Shirley's classroom at [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), he quickly warmed to her, cheering her up with wild orchids on her first day of teaching and sharing a composition about his imaginary rock friends at the shore. At the end of the school year, Paul joined [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) in the graveyard, where they shared their thoughts on memory, grief, and imagination. [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) later visited Paul for tea in his grandmother's absence, reassuring him regarding his imaginative nature. Later, Paul accompanied [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to [Echo Lodge](../codex/places.md#echo-lodge), where he bonded with Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) over their shared experiences with imaginary dream-people. Years later, he returned to [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) as one of the guests attending Anne's wedding to [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md).

_Sources: [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P0](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0000), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P13](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0013), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P20](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0020), [v2 XI Facts and Fancies P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 XI Facts and Fancies P42](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0042), +26 more_

## Quotes

> "and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . ."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)

> “Yes; but if dryads are foolish they must take the consequences, just as if they were real people,” said Paul gravely. “Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.”
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P30](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0030)

> "I’ve eaten enough to make anyone grow. I do hope, now that I’ve begun, I’ll keep on till I’m as tall as father. He is six feet, you know, Miss Lavendar."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024)

> "I think you would make a splendid mother. You have just the right look in your eyes . . . the look my little mother always had. I think it’s a pity you haven’t any boys of your own."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P58](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0058)

> "He knows I won’t associate with him if he doesn’t. He is really full of wickedness, I think."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XV The Beginning of Vacation P14](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0014)

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--paul-irving.md)

Paul is a student of [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), who acts as an influential teacher to him. Beyond the classroom, they are kindred spirits and confidants who share deep conversations about memory, grief, and their imaginative ideas. Paul enjoys spending time with her, such as inviting her for tea or joining her for walks in the graveyard.
